Musculotendon actuators

Source: R/physics-biomechanics-musculotendon.R
musculotendon.Rd

Musculotendon models after SymPy's MusculotendonDeGroote2016: a force actuator along a pathway whose force follows from the activation dynamics, the characteristic curves of De Groote et al. (2016) and the chosen MusculotendonFormulation(). Constants left as NULL become symbols named after the model. The rigid tendon formulation and the explicit fiber length and tendon force formulations are available; the implicit ones raise NotImplementedError as in SymPy. MusculotendonDeGroote2016_with_defaults() uses the published curve constants and default fiber velocity, pennation and damping values. MusculotendonBase() is the abstract base class and raises an error.

Usage

MusculotendonBase(...)

MusculotendonDeGroote2016(
  name,
  pathway,
  activation_dynamics,
  musculotendon_dynamics = 0L,
  tendon_slack_length = NULL,
  peak_isometric_force = NULL,
  optimal_fiber_length = NULL,
  maximal_fiber_velocity = NULL,
  optimal_pennation_angle = NULL,
  fiber_damping_coefficient = NULL,
  with_defaults = FALSE
)

MusculotendonDeGroote2016_with_defaults(
  name,
  pathway,
  activation_dynamics,
  musculotendon_dynamics = 0L,
  tendon_slack_length = NULL,
  peak_isometric_force = NULL,
  optimal_fiber_length = NULL,
  maximal_fiber_velocity = Float("10.0"),
  optimal_pennation_angle = Float("0.0"),
  fiber_damping_coefficient = Float("0.1")
)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

name

Name of the musculotendon.

pathway

A pathway, such as LinearPathway().

activation_dynamics

An activation model, such as FirstOrderActivationDeGroote2016().

musculotendon_dynamics

A MusculotendonFormulation() value.

tendon_slack_length, peak_isometric_force, optimal_fiber_length, maximal_fiber_velocity, optimal_pennation_angle, fiber_damping_coefficient

Model constants.

with_defaults

Use the published curve constants.

Value

A musculotendon object.

Details

The objects expose SymPy's attributes through $, among them force, pathway, activation_dynamics, state_vars (x), input_vars (r), constants (p), M, F, rhs() and to_loads().

Examples

N <- ReferenceFrame("N")
O <- PhysPoint("O"); I <- PhysPoint("I")
I$set_pos(O, dynamicsymbols("q") * N$x)
muscle <- MusculotendonDeGroote2016("m", LinearPathway(O, I), FirstOrderActivationDeGroote2016("m"))
muscle$x
#> Matrix(1, 1)
#> [a_m(t)]
muscle$constants
#> Matrix(31, 1)
